                    text: [32m'# Vector Search - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-03-31, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.24.1/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2024-09-24, last updated: 2026-04-10, [Read more](https://www.samrat.fyi/projects/vector)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The best thing about Typesense is - once schema is created with vector fields Typesense automatically uses each fields to generate vector values by using OPENAI API.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The vector fields are only valid with string type and each vector values are the collection of string fields mentioned inside vector fields when creating schema and looks like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The num_dim parameter in vector fields as mentioned in schema specifies the number of dimensions of the vector.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It tells Typesense how many float values are present in each vector used for vector search in our case, 1536.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'{\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"exclude_fields": "vectors",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"page": 1,\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Summary of Workflow:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Typesense will automatically use the ML model you specified when creating the schema to generate and store embeddings for each of your JSON documents.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'To do a semantic search, we just have to add the\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In many cases, you might want to combine keyword searches along with semantic search.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'You can do this in Typesense, by adding a keyword field name to\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense will do a keyword search on all the regular fields, and a semantic search on the auto-embedding field and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'combine the results using Rank Fusion to arrive at a **fusion score** that is used to rank the hits.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense will do a keyword search using the `q` parameter, and a nearest neighbor search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using the `vector_query` field and combine the results into a ranked set of results using rank fusion as described earlier.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### # Re-ranking Hybrid Matches\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, during hybrid search:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through keyword search but not through vector search will only have a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through vector search but not through keyword search will only have a vector distance score\n'[39m +

                      [32m'When enabled:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through keyword search will also get a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through vector search will also get a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This allows for more comprehensive ranking of results, at the cost of additional computation time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also set a maximum vector distance threshold for results of semantic search and hybrid search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When doing hybrid search, by default Typesense returns both keyword matches and semantic matches in the results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through keyword search but not through vector search will only have a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through vector search but not through keyword search will only have a vector distance score\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rerank_hybrid_matches: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. When enabled:- Documents found only through keyword search will also get a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through vector search will also get a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example with re-ranking enabled:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-27, [Read more](https://docs-python.ru/other/polnotekstovyi-poisk-s-typesense/gibridnyi-ranking-keyword-vector-search/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense выполняет keyword search по обычным полям, semantic search по embedding-полю и объединяет результаты через rank fusion.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'В hybrid search часть документов может быть найдена только keyword-поиском, а часть - только vector-поиском.\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building a Hybrid Document Search Engine with Typesense and LLMs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://surya-digital.com/blog/2025-08-13/rag-powered-search-index)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports hybrid search out of the box.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The system uses a combination of text and vector search to retrieve relevant documents:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. `q` - The search query text, with notes about wildcard usage\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": query,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `run_query_llm` function orchestrates the entire search and response generation process through several key steps:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Step 1: Vector Database Search**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'**Step 2: Image Generation from PDF Pages**'[39m

                      [32m'Typesense is a single search engine that handles all of the above.\n'[39m +

                      [32m"# Hybrid search with remote embedding doesn't return relevant keyword results.\n"[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to implement semantic search for a forum? - Forums - BaseHub\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-01-07, last updated: 2026-04-02, [Read more](https://forums.basehub.com/typesense/typesense/1)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**What it does:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Combines keyword/full-text search WITH semantic similarity in a single query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Users get both exact matches AND conceptually related posts\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Much better UX since users don't need to choose between search modes\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Set up your collection with vector field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Index your posts (embeddings auto-generated)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await client.collections("forum_posts").documents().create(post);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Hybrid search query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const results = await client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.collections("forum_posts")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.documents()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.search({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'q: "best practices for async JavaScript",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query_by: "title,content", // Full-text search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'vector_query: "content_embedding", // Semantic search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'limit: 20\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Results will be ranked by hybrid score (combines BM25 + vector similarity)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Put exact keyword matches first (they're usually what users want)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Let Typesense handle the ranking automatically via hybrid scoring\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- A single search box\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'd have to:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'1. Make API calls to Vercel AI Gateway yourself\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Store the embeddings in Typesense as `float[]` fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Query using `vector_query`'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# You can perform hybrid search What I mean is it should be li typesense #community-help\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-07, last updated: 2025-08-03, [Read more](https://threads.typesense.org/t/29444780/you-can-perform-hybrid-search-what-i-mean-is-it-should-be-li)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This should perform a hybrid search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'search_requests = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'searches': [\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'collection': collection_name,\n"[39m +
                      [32m`'query_by': "content",\n`[39m +
                      [32m`'q': "liste des congés",\n`[39m +
                      [32m"'prefix': 'false',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'vector_query': f'embedding:({query_emebedding},distance_threshold:0.5)',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'# <=== Be sure to replace `embedding` with the name of the field that stores your embeddings.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'exclude_fields': 'embedding'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"# <=== Don't return the raw floating point numbers in the vector field in the search API response, to save on network bandwidth.\n"[39m +

                      [32m'search_results = client.multi_search.perform(search_requests, common_search_params)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As of `v28.0`, Typesense provides a `union` feature that allows you to merge search results from multiple collections into a single, ordered set of hits.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'`float[]` field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`num_dim` property for indexing them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`num_dim` property specifies the number of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'dimensions (length of the float array) that your embeddings contain.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's create a collection called\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can set\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`ef_construction` (default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`200`) and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`M` (default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`16`) for vector and embedding fields while creating\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the collection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "docs",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "vec",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"num_dim": 768,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"hnsw_params": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"ef_construction": 100,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"M": 8\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using Typesense for embeddings search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-28, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/vector_databases/typesense/using_typesense_for_embeddings_search)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To index vectors in Typesense, we’ll first create a Collection (which is a collection of Documents) and turn on vector indexing for a particular field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can even store multiple vector fields in a single document.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"typesense_client.collections['wikipedia_articles'].delete()\n"[39m +
                      [32m'except Exception as e:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pass\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Create a new collection\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "content_vector",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +

                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`"num_dim": len(article_df['title_vector'][0])\n`[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create_response = typesense_client.collections.create(schema)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'print(create_response)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'print("Created new collection wikipedia-articles")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Поиск с Typesense: векторный поиск, embeddings и ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-01, [Read more](https://docs-python.ru/other/polnotekstovyi-poisk-s-typesense/vektornyi-poisk-i-gibridnyi-ranking/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'В примере `embedding` объявлен как `float[]`, а `num_dim` фиксирует размерность вектора.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Для учебного материала используется `num_dim: 4`, чтобы код был коротким.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Создание коллекции\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def recreate_collection(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client: typesense.Client,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema: dict[str, Any],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'drop_existing: bool = False,\n'[39m +
                      [32m') -> None:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection_name = schema["name"]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if drop_existing:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'try:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client.collections[collection_name].delete()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'except typesense.exceptions.ObjectNotFound:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pass\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client.collections.create(schema)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Collections & Data | Fluent-Health/typesense | Providers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-27, [Read more](https://library.tf/providers/Fluent-Health/typesense/latest/docs/resources/collection)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Terraform will still remove auto-created fields for collections with auto-type, so you need to manually update the collection schema to match generated fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Schema\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Required\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `name` (String) Collection name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Nested Schema for fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Required:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `name` (String)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `type` (String) Field type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Optional:\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- `async_reference` (Boolean) Allow documents to be indexed successfully even when the referenced document doesn't exist yet.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Only meaningful when `reference` is set.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to false.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Defaults to true.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to empty string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `num_dim` (Number) Number of dimensions for vector fields (float[] type).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Required for manual vector search fields; auto-computed by the server for auto-embedded fields (from the embedder's output dimension).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- `optional` (Boolean) Optional field.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Support for lower precision types for embeddings vectors, like fp16 ...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Create a collection like\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vector Search with Text Embeddings Models in Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-24, last updated: 2026-04-10, [Read more](https://www.samrat.fyi/projects/vector)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'{\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The num_dim parameter in vector fields as mentioned in schema specifies the number of dimensions of the vector.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +

Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes.             [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +

            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +

            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.                     text: [32m'# Vector Search - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-03-31, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.24.1/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports the ability to add embeddings generated by your Machine Learning models to each document, and then doing a nearest-neighbor search on them.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vector Search with Text Embeddings Models in Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-24, last updated: 2026-04-10, [Read more](https://www.samrat.fyi/projects/vector)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The best thing about Typesense is - once schema is created with vector fields Typesense automatically uses each fields to generate vector values by using OPENAI API.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The vector fields are only valid with string type and each vector values are the collection of string fields mentioned inside vector fields when creating schema and looks like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The num_dim parameter in vector fields as mentioned in schema specifies the number of dimensions of the vector.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It tells Typesense how many float values are present in each vector used for vector search in our case, 1536.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Prepare search request\n'[39m +
                      [32m'search_parameters = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"searches": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"collection": "person",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"exclude_fields": "vectors",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"page": 1,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"per_page": 100,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"vector_query": vector_query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Summary of Workflow:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'2. Define a schema in Typesense with a vector field (embedding).\n'[39m +

                      [32m'4. Index the person data with the vector embeddings.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. Perform vector searches by comparing query embeddings to stored embeddings.'[39m

                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/semantic-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense will automatically use the ML model you specified when creating the schema to generate and store embeddings for each of your JSON documents.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do a semantic search, we just have to add the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m"}'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In many cases, you might want to combine keyword searches along with semantic search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call this Hybrid Search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can do this in Typesense, by adding a keyword field name to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m', in addition to the auto-embedding field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When doing hybrid search, by default Typesense returns both keyword matches and semantic matches in the results.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Для vector search в документе появляется специальное поле:\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Vector Search and Embeddings\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense will do a keyword search on all the regular fields, and a semantic search on the auto-embedding field and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'combine the results using Rank Fusion to arrive at a **fusion score** that is used to rank the hits.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense will do a keyword search using the `q` parameter, and a nearest neighbor search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using the `vector_query` field and combine the results into a ranked set of results using rank fusion as described earlier.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### # Re-ranking Hybrid Matches\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, during hybrid search:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through keyword search but not through vector search will only have a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through vector search but not through keyword search will only have a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can optionally compute both scores for all matches by setting `rerank_hybrid_matches: true` in your search parameters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When enabled:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through keyword search will also get a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through vector search will also get a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This allows for more comprehensive ranking of results, at the cost of additional computation time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also set a maximum vector distance threshold for results of semantic search and hybrid search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'sorting clause for reordering keyword search hits.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Semantic Search with OpenAI and Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/semantic-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When doing hybrid search, by default Typesense returns both keyword matches and semantic matches in the results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through keyword search but not through vector search will only have a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found through vector search but not through keyword search will only have a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can optionally compute both scores for all matches by setting\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rerank_hybrid_matches: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. When enabled:- Documents found only through keyword search will also get a vector distance score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Documents found only through vector search will also get a text match score\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example with re-ranking enabled:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m' -H "X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY: ${TYPESENSE_API_KEY}" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m' -X POST \\\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-27, [Read more](https://docs-python.ru/other/polnotekstovyi-poisk-s-typesense/gibridnyi-ranking-keyword-vector-search/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense выполняет keyword search по обычным полям, semantic search по embedding-полю и объединяет результаты через rank fusion.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'В hybrid search часть документов может быть найдена только keyword-поиском, а часть - только vector-поиском.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building a Hybrid Document Search Engine with Typesense and LLMs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://surya-digital.com/blog/2025-08-13/rag-powered-search-index)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports hybrid search out of the box.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The system uses a combination of text and vector search to retrieve relevant documents:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. `q` - The search query text, with notes about wildcard usage\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- Alpha parameter for balancing semantic vs keyword search weights.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": query,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `run_query_llm` function orchestrates the entire search and response generation process through several key steps:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Step 1: Vector Database Search**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'results = run_query_on_vector_db(search_utils=search_utils, query=query, number_of_results=number_of_results)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This calls the Typesense hybrid search with the following process:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- Uses the `alpha` parameter (default 0.9) to weight semantic vs keyword matching\n'[39m +

                      [32m'**Step 2: Image Generation from PDF Pages**'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense is a single search engine that handles all of the above.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"**Your current situation**: You're forced to pick between vector databases (semantic but no keywords) or keyword search (exact matches but no understanding).\n"[39m +

                      [32m"# Hybrid search with remote embedding doesn't return relevant keyword results.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to implement semantic search for a forum? - Forums - BaseHub\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-01-07, last updated: 2026-04-02, [Read more](https://forums.basehub.com/typesense/typesense/1)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**What it does:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Combines keyword/full-text search WITH semantic similarity in a single query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Users get both exact matches AND conceptually related posts\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Much better UX since users don't need to choose between search modes\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Set up your collection with vector field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Index your posts (embeddings auto-generated)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await client.collections("forum_posts").documents().create(post);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Hybrid search query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const results = await client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.collections("forum_posts")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.documents()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.search({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'q: "best practices for async JavaScript",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query_by: "title,content", // Full-text search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'vector_query: "content_embedding", // Semantic search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'limit: 20\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Results will be ranked by hybrid score (combines BM25 + vector similarity)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Put exact keyword matches first (they're usually what users want)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Let Typesense handle the ranking automatically via hybrid scoring\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- A single search box\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'1. Make API calls to Vercel AI Gateway yourself\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Store the embeddings in Typesense as `float[]` fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Query using `vector_query`'[39m

                    text: [32m'# You can perform hybrid search What I mean is it should be li typesense #community-help\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-07, last updated: 2025-08-03, [Read more](https://threads.typesense.org/t/29444780/you-can-perform-hybrid-search-what-i-mean-is-it-should-be-li)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This should perform a hybrid search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'search_requests = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'searches': [\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'collection': collection_name,\n"[39m +
                      [32m`'query_by': "content",\n`[39m +
                      [32m`'q': "liste des congés",\n`[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vector Search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-08-27, last updated: 2024-11-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/26.0/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once your document embeddings are ready, you want to create a collection that contains a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`float[]` field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`num_dim` property for indexing them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`num_dim` property specifies the number of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'dimensions (length of the float array) that your embeddings contain.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's create a collection called\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can set\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`ef_construction` (default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`200`) and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`M` (default:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`16`) for vector and embedding fields while creating\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the collection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "docs",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "vec",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"num_dim": 768,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"hnsw_params": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"ef_construction": 100,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"M": 8\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using Typesense for embeddings search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-28, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/vector_databases/typesense/using_typesense_for_embeddings_search)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To index vectors in Typesense, we’ll first create a Collection (which is a collection of Documents) and turn on vector indexing for a particular field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can even store multiple vector fields in a single document.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"typesense_client.collections['wikipedia_articles'].delete()\n"[39m +
                      [32m'except Exception as e:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pass\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Create a new collection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "wikipedia_articles",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "content_vector",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`"num_dim": len(article_df['content_vector'][0])\n`[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "title_vector",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`"num_dim": len(article_df['title_vector'][0])\n`[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create_response = typesense_client.collections.create(schema)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'print(create_response)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'print("Created new collection wikipedia-articles")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Created new collection wikipedia-articles\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Поиск с Typesense: векторный поиск, embeddings и ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-01, [Read more](https://docs-python.ru/other/polnotekstovyi-poisk-s-typesense/vektornyi-poisk-i-gibridnyi-ranking/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'В примере `embedding` объявлен как `float[]`, а `num_dim` фиксирует размерность вектора.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Для учебного материала используется `num_dim: 4`, чтобы код был коротким.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'В production размерность должна совпадать с выбранной embedding-моделью.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Создание коллекции\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def recreate_collection(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client: typesense.Client,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema: dict[str, Any],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'drop_existing: bool = False,\n'[39m +
                      [32m') -> None:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection_name = schema["name"]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if drop_existing:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'try:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client.collections[collection_name].delete()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'except typesense.exceptions.ObjectNotFound:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pass\n'[39m +
                      [32m'client.collections.create(schema)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Collections & Data | Fluent-Health/typesense | Providers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-27, [Read more](https://library.tf/providers/Fluent-Health/typesense/latest/docs/resources/collection)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Terraform will still remove auto-created fields for collections with auto-type, so you need to manually update the collection schema to match generated fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Schema\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Required\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `name` (String) Collection name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Optional\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Nested Schema for fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Required:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `name` (String)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `type` (String) Field type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Optional:\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- `async_reference` (Boolean) Allow documents to be indexed successfully even when the referenced document doesn't exist yet.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Only meaningful when `reference` is set.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to false.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to true.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to empty string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `num_dim` (Number) Number of dimensions for vector fields (float[] type).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Required for manual vector search fields; auto-computed by the server for auto-embedded fields (from the embedder's output dimension).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- `optional` (Boolean) Optional field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to false.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `range_index` (Boolean) Enables an index optimized for range filtering on numerical fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Defaults to false.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `reference` (String) Name of a field in another collection that should be linked to this collection so that it can be joined during query (e.g. "users.id").'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Support for lower precision types for embeddings vectors, like fp16 ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-04-22, last updated: 2025-09-22, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/1684)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Create a collection like\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'places',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'fields' => [\n"[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'title',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'string'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'points',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'int32'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'embedding',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'float[]',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'num_dim' => 4\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'default_sorting_field' => 'points'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Users can define a schema using\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'places',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'fields' => [\n"[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'title',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'string'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'points',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'int32'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'embedding',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'float16[]',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'num_dim' => 4\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'default_sorting_field' => 'points'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'title',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'embedding',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'type' => 'float16[]',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'float16\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'is not a valid type for a field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Vector Search with Text Embeddings Models in Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-24, last updated: 2026-04-10, [Read more](https://www.samrat.fyi/projects/vector)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "person",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "id", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "name", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "age", "type": "int32"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "description", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "email", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "vector",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"type": "float[]",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"num_dim":1536,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"embed": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"from": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"age",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"description",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"email"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The num_dim parameter in vector fields as mentioned in schema specifies the number of dimensions of the vector.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It tells Typesense how many float values are present in each vector used for vector search in our case, 1536.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Summary of Workflow:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Generate embeddings using OpenAI’s text-embedding-ada-002 model for each person.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Define a schema in Typesense with a vector field (embedding).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Create a persons collection in Typesense.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Index the person data with the vector embeddings.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. Perform vector searches by comparing query embeddings to stored embeddings.'[39m
                  },

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.
